hypothesis: Small span-smoothing of noisy priors may improve path estimates under some error structures; quantify harms under non-span/sparse/correlated counterexamples before considering any real candidate.
algorithm: Fit fixed ridge1 span spline to supplied noisy prior; blend original prior with smoothed prior by fixed0/.05/.1/.25; each solves the same nonnegative official lambda.05 objective.
calibration: Truth draws independent of released b, scaled to released train median link load. Additive noise scale uses train-only count-covariance path variance estimate; low/high multipliers .5/2. Multiplicative logsigma .35/.8; origin/destination correlated log factors .25/.6.
selection: None. All methods and harms reported, no best synthetic model promoted; original official Task4 baseline unchanged.
scope: Artificial sensitivity, not hidden path validation. Actual priors have positive continuous values with no observed zero atom; clipped Gaussian stress is explicitly a counter-assumption, not claimed true generation. No Kaggle upload.
